On January 31, Argentina published the resolution for its next renewable auction, after a four-year hiatus. The process awarded a total of 634MW and focused on small renewable projects with up to 20MW capacity. CAMMESA, the power market administrator, allocated a maximum capacity per region, as the country faces transmission bottlenecks. The auction targeted solar with and without storage, wind with storage, biomass, and small hydro. The government will received bids on April 27 and awarded projects on July 24. Solar and wind projects paired with batteries secured offtake agreements for the first time. Solar was by far the most awarded technology, with 450MW, or 71% of total capacity.
